name: Primary Renal Tubular Acidosis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Primary Renal Tubular Acidosis

criteria.description: Presence of normal anion gap metabolic acidosis with hyperchloremia
Inappropriately high urine pH (>5.5) despite systemic acidemia
Hypokalemia or low serum potassium levels
Exclusion of secondary causes of renal tubular acidosis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of normal anion gap metabolic acidosis with hyperchloremia, inappropriately high urine pH despite systemic acidemia, and exclusion of secondary causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis in familial cases

searchTerms: acid-base imbalance with normal anion gap
metabolic acidosis without increased anion gap

pathognomonic.symptomName: Inappropriately alkaline urine pH (>5.5) during systemic acidemia
searchTerms: urine is too alkaline despite body acidemia
high urine pH during systemic acidosis
weak muscles due to potassium loss
weakness related to salt or mineral problems
low blood pressure due to dehydration
irregular heartbeats caused by low potassium

rare.symptomName: Sensorineural hearing loss (in some genetic subtypes)

laboratory: Normal anion gap metabolic acidosis with hyperchloremia
Inappropriately high urine pH (>5.5) despite systemic acidemia
imaging: Renal ultrasound showing nephrocalcinosis or nephrolithiasis
Bone X-rays showing signs of osteomalacia or rickets
genetic: Mutations in genes such as SLC4A1, ATP6V1B1, ATP6V0A4 depending on subtype
other: Positive family history in inherited cases

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of underlying systemic disease (e.g. autoimmune disorders, medications)
Resolution after treatment of underlying cause

redFlags: Severe hypokalemia causing muscle paralysis or arrhythmias
Failure to thrive or severe growth retardation in children
Nephrocalcinosis leading to progressive renal impairment
references: Batlle DC, Haque SK. Genetic causes and mechanisms of distal renal tubular acidosis. Nephrol Dial Transplant. 2012;27(10):3691-3704.
Orphanet: Primary renal tubular acidosis - ORPHA:314822
Karet FE. Inherited distal renal tubular acidosis. J Am Soc Nephrol. 2001;12(8):1548-1557.
